chosen_property.label: location
chosen_property.justification: schema:location directly expresses an event occurring in a place.

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: deathPlace
candidates.comment: A geographical event relation between a person and the place where they died. Also called: place of demise, passing location, decease location. Examples: "Historical Figure" death place "Dallas, Texas", "Family Member" death place "London, UK". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the place of birth.

candidates.label: sportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A specific location relation between an exercise action and the sports activity venue where it took place. Also called "exercise location", "training venue", "athletic facility", "gym location". Examples: "The run had sportsActivityLocation Central Park", "The workout's sportsActivityLocation was the local gym", "This exercise action took place at a sportsActivityLocation stadium.". Distinct from location, which is a more general location property.

candidates.label: spatial
candidates.comment: A general spatial relation between a creative work and a place, used when more specific location properties are not applicable. Also called "related to place", "takes place in", "associated location", "geographic context". Examples: "The novel has spatial Paris", "The painting's spatial is a rural landscape", "This document's spatial is the Amazon rainforest.". Distinct from spatialCoverage, which indicates the specific geographic focus of the content.

candidates.label: studyLocation
candidates.comment: A geographic relation between a medical study and the administrative area where it is conducted or was conducted. Also called "research location", "trial site", "study area", "geographic scope of study". Examples: "The medical study has studyLocation New York", "The clinical trial's studyLocation is Europe", "This study is taking place in a specific studyLocation."

candidates.label: geo
candidates.comment: A geo relation between a place and its geographical coordinates or shape. Also called: geographic location, coordinates, spatial data. Examples: "Eiffel Tower" geo "Latitude: 48.8584, Longitude: 2.2945", "Central Park" geo "Polygon GeoShape", "Mount Everest" geo "Point GeoCoordinates".

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: sportsEvent
candidates.comment: A specific event relation between an exercise action and the sports event during which it occurred. Also called "event of exercise", "competition event", "athletic event". Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: legalRepresentative

candidates.label: performerIn

Examples: John Doe is a performer in 'The Annual Gala'. Jane Smith is a performer in 'The City Marathon'. An actor is a performer in 'The New Play'. Distinct from performer, which points from an event to a person.

candidates.label: agent
candidates.comment: An agent relation between an action and the organization or person who directly performs or drives it. Also called performer, doer, initiator, actor. Examples: "A 'write book' action's agent is 'John Doe'.", "A 'deliver package' action's agent is 'Delivery Service Inc'."

candidates.label: representativeOfPage
candidates.comment: A representative of page relation indicating whether an image object accurately reflects the content of the web page it appears on. Also called page representative, content summary image. Examples: "A thumbnail image is representative of page 'true'.", "A decorative image is representative of page 'false'.", "A product photo is representative of page 'true'."

candidates.label: contributor

Also called "additional contributor", "supporting role", "collaborator". Examples: "Book creative work contributor 'Editor Jane Doe'", "Conference event contributor 'Sponsor Acme Corp'". Distinct from author or creator, which typically denote primary responsibility.

candidates.label: buyer
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sell action, indicating the organization or person who purchased the object. Also called "purchaser", "customer", "acquired by". Examples: "Online purchase sell action buyer Jane Doe", "Company acquisition sell action buyer Acme Corp". Distinct from seller, which is the party offering the object for sale.

candidates.label: nationality

Examples: "Person A nationality 'United States'", "Person B nationality 'France'", "Person C nationality 'Japan'". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the location where a person was born.

candidates.label: sponsor

Also called "funded by", "supported by", "patron", "underwritten by". Examples: "The event has sponsor Acme Corp", "The medical study's sponsor is the NIH", "This artist has sponsor a private foundation."

candidates.label: recipient

candidates.label: relatedTo

candidates.label: measuredProperty

candidates.label: timeRequired

candidates.comment: A type of good relation between ownership information or a type and quantity node and the product or service it refers to. Also called product type, service type, item type. Examples: "OwnershipInfo typeOfGood 'Car'", "TypeAndQuantityNode typeOfGood 'Laptop'", "OwnershipInfo typeOfGood 'Software License'".

candidates.label: priceType
candidates.comment: A categorical attribute defining the specific type of a price, such as a list price, sale price, or manufacturer suggested retail price. Also called pricing category, cost classification, rate type. Examples: A unit price specification has a price type of 'ListPrice'. A price has a price type of 'SalePrice'. The product's price type is 'MSRP'.

candidates.label: sport
candidates.comment: An identification of the type of sport associated with a sports event or organization. Also called "sport type", "athletic discipline", "game played". Examples: "The event's sport is Basketball", "The organization's sport is Soccer", "This competition features the sport of Gymnastics."

candidates.label: category
candidates.comment: A classification relation assigning a category to an item such as an offer, product, service, or announcement. Also called "type", "classification", "genre", "tag". Examples: "Product category 'Electronics'", "Service category 'Home Repair'", "Offer category 'Seasonal Sale'".

candidates.label: structuralClass
candidates.comment: A classification of a joint based on how bones physically connect to each other. Also called "joint classification", "bone connection type", "anatomical joint type". Examples: "The knee joint has structuralClass synovial", "The skull sutures have structuralClass fibrous", "This joint's structuralClass is cartilaginous."

chosen_property.label: hasTemporalSequence
chosen_property.definition: Indicates a temporal relationship where one event precedes or follows another.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property directly expresses one event preceding another event.

candidates.label: previousItem
candidates.comment: A sequential relation between a list item and the list item that immediately precedes it. Also called precedes, comes after, follows. Examples: List item 'B' has a previous item 'A'. The current item's previous item is the one before it. In a breadcrumb trail, the current page has a previous item. Distinct from nextItem, which links to the item that follows.

candidates.label: successorOf
candidates.comment: A lineage relation between a newer product model and its previous, often discontinued, predecessor. Also called "replaces", "evolved from", "preceded by", "derived from". Examples: "iPhone 15 is successorOf iPhone 14", "The new car model is successorOf the previous generation", "This product is a successorOf an older variant."

candidates.label: nextItem
candidates.comment: A list item that immediately follows the current list item in an ordered sequence. Also called subsequent item, following item, next in list. Examples: "Item 1 nextItem 'Item 2'", "Page 3 nextItem 'Page 4'", "Step A nextItem 'Step B'". Distinct from previousItem, which links to the preceding item.

candidates.label: previousStartDate
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the previously scheduled start date for an event that has been rescheduled or cancelled. Also called original start date, former start date, initial event date. Examples: A rescheduled event has a previous start date of '2023-03-15'. The cancelled concert had a previous start date of '2023-07-01T19:00:00'. The postponed meeting's previous start date was 'last Monday'. Distinct from startDate, which is the current or newly scheduled start date.

candidates.label: beforeMedia
candidates.comment: A media object representing the circumstances prior to performing a how-to direction. Also called: pre-action media, initial state media. Examples: "HowToDirection 'Install Shelf' beforeMedia 'Image of empty wall'", "HowToDirection 'Bake Cake' beforeMedia 'Video of ingredients on counter'."

candidates.label: dateReceived
candidates.comment: A temporal arrival relation between a message and the date/time it was received by the recipient. Also called: reception date, message arrival time, delivery time. Examples: "Email" date received "2023-10-26T10:25:00Z", "Package Notification" date received "2023-10-26T11:00:00Z". Distinct from dateSent, which is when the message was dispatched.

candidates.label: supersededBy
candidates.comment: A deprecation relation between an older term (property, class, or enumeration) and a newer term that replaces or supersedes it. Also called "replaced by", "obsoleted by", "succeeded by", "deprecated by". Examples: "OldProperty is supersededBy NewProperty", "The deprecated class is supersededBy a modern equivalent", "This enumeration value is supersededBy a more precise one."

candidates.label: datePublished
candidates.comment: A temporal release relation between a certification or creative work and its date of first publication or broadcast. Also called: publication date, broadcast date, release date. Examples: "Book" date published "1984-06-08", "TV Show Episode" date published "2023-01-01", "Certification" date published "2022-12-01". Distinct from dateCreated, which is the date of creation, and datePosted, which is for online listings.

candidates.label: predecessorOf
candidates.comment: A lineage relation between a product model and its newer, often superseding, variant. Also called replaced by, succeeded by, updated to, newer version is. Examples: iPhone 10 is a predecessor of iPhone 11. Model A is a predecessor of Model B. The old software version is a predecessor of the new one. Distinct from successorOf, which points from a newer variant to an older one.

candidates.label: dateDeleted
candidates.comment: A temporal removal relation between a data feed item and the datetime it was removed from the feed. Also called: deletion date, removal date, date of removal. Examples: "Expired Job Posting" date deleted "2023-06-30", "Outdated Product Listing" date deleted "2023-01-01T00:00:00Z".

chosen_property.label: precededByDuration
chosen_property.definition: Indicates the duration of time that elapsed before an event.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property directly expresses an event being preceded by a specific duration.

candidates.label: duration
candidates.comment: A duration relation between an item (such as an event, media object, or schedule) and its length of time. Also called "length", "time span", "period". Examples: "Movie 'Avatar' duration 'PT2H42M'", "Event 'Concert' duration 'PT3H'", "Audio recording duration 'PT5M30S'". Distinct from durationOfWarranty, which is specifically about warranty length.

candidates.label: durationOfWarranty
candidates.comment: A warranty duration relation between a warranty promise and the quantitative value representing its length. Also called "warranty period", "guarantee length", "coverage duration". Examples: "Laptop warranty durationOfWarranty 'P1Y'", "Car warranty durationOfWarranty 'P3Y'", "Appliance warranty durationOfWarranty 'P6M'". Distinct from duration, which is a general property for the length of various items.

candidates.label: deliveryTime
candidates.comment: A temporal duration relation between delivery time settings or offer shipping details and the total delay from order receipt to goods reaching the final customer. Also called: total delivery time, shipping duration, estimated delivery. Examples: "Standard Shipping" delivery time "5-7 business days", "Express Delivery" delivery time "1-2 days", "International Shipment" delivery time "2-3 weeks". Distinct from deliveryLeadTime, which is the time until dispatch or pickup readiness.

candidates.label: cookTime
candidates.comment: A temporal measurement for a recipe, indicating the duration required to cook the dish. Also called "cooking duration", "preparation time", "time to cook". Examples: "Recipe 'Chicken Curry' cookTime 'PT30M'", "Recipe 'Cake' cookTime 'PT45M'". Distinct from prepTime, which is the time for preparation before cooking, and totalTime, which is the sum of all time.

candidates.label: termDuration
candidates.comment: A duration representing the length of a term of study within an educational or occupational program. Also called "term length", "semester duration", "quarter length", "study period duration". Examples: "The program has termDuration 15 weeks", "The educational program's termDuration is 10 weeks", "This course has a termDuration of one semester."

candidates.label: timeToComplete
candidates.comment: A duration representing the expected length of time to complete an educational or occupational program when attending full-time. Also called "program duration", "completion duration", "full-time study length", "expected completion time". Examples: "The degree program has timeToComplete 4 years", "The certification's timeToComplete is 6 months", "This program requires timeToComplete 2 years of full-time study."

candidates.label: loanTerm
candidates.comment: A loan duration relation between a loan or credit and the quantitative value representing its agreement term. Also called: loan duration, credit term, repayment period. Examples: "Car Loan loanTerm '60 months'", "Mortgage loanTerm '30 years'", "Personal Loan loanTerm '5 years'".

candidates.label: activityDuration
candidates.comment: An activity duration relation between an exercise plan and the length of time recommended for engaging in the activity. Also called exercise length, workout time, session duration. Examples: "An exercise plan's activity duration is '30 minutes'.", "The yoga routine's activity duration is '1 hour'."

candidates.label: prepTime
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the duration required to prepare items for use in instructions or a direction. Also called preparation duration, setup time, readiness time. Examples: A recipe has a prep time of 'PT15M'. A DIY project has a prep time of 'PT30M'. A cooking instruction has a prep time of 'PT10M'. Distinct from performTime, which is the time to execute the instructions.

candidates.label: timeRequired
candidates.comment: A duration representing the approximate time typically needed for an audience to engage with or complete a creative work. Also called "completion time", "estimated duration", "reading time", "viewing time". Examples: "The article has timeRequired 10 minutes", "The course's timeRequired is 40 hours", "This creative work takes timeRequired 2 hours to watch."
